what: CORROBORATION, not a performance claim. The parity probe of portal_submit_review_decision (an all-zero request_id), timed across the five committed parity runs, is independent evidence that fix (c)'s check 0 (the approver check) runs before anything is read. Until now, that ordering was established by two things: code inspection (src/reviewer_portal/decisions.py, submit_decision) and the structural test tests/test_approvers_portal.py::test_check_0_runs_first_and_has_no_default, which asserts that require_approver is the first statement. Timing corroborates it by a different route: it looks at the running system's behaviour, not its source.

primary_evidence.design: A within-run control. The same probe was sent in the same run, at the same moment, to the same source: the deployed portal at d7bad89, and the runner's in-process portal, which also ran d7bad89 server code. Only one thing differed. The deployed side's caller (the runner SP) is not a listed approver, so check 0 refused it. The in-process side ran as the test approver (the conftest fixture defect, since fixed in 6056f37), so it passed check 0.
primary_evidence.result: Refused at check 0: 28 ms (deployed; portal log line 20:43:52Z, reason not_in_set). Passed check 0 and reached the not-found check, a warehouse read: 421 ms (in-process).
primary_evidence.why_it_isolates: It spans no commits and no days, and the transport bias runs against the result. In every pre-fix run the in-process side is the FASTER one (306-362 ms in-process vs 398-505 ms deployed), because it skips the Apps HTTP round trip. Here the in-process side is 15x slower, and the extra time is the work behind check 0.

supporting_evidence: The cross-run comparison below: pre-fix runs (398-505 ms deployed, 306-362 ms in-process) against the check-0 refusals in 7f3b2f82 and 47501246 (28-42 ms deployed, 3 ms in-process). It agrees with the primary evidence, but it spans commits and days, so it is support, not the primary result.
source: Per-case lines in each run's report.log (eval/results/runs/*_parity_*/report.log), parsed with scripts/export_evidence.py CASE_RE. Format: outcome remote/in-process, bytes, remote_ms/inprocess_ms.
probe: portal_submit_review_decision {decision: approved, rationale: 'parity probe: request does not exist', request_id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, reviewer_id: demo_sia, an active persona} (tests/test_parity.py, NO_SUCH_REQUEST). It passes every input check (persona, decision, rationale, corrections), so without check 0 the first refusal is check 5, 'No review request', which needs data.request_by_id, a warehouse query.

runs.path: both sides reach check 5 (warehouse read, not found)

deployed: refused at check 0 (runner SP not listed; portal log line 20:43:52Z, not_in_set). In-process: ran as the test approver (conftest fixture defect, since fixed), passed check 0 and reached check 5. The run FAILED parity because the two sides differed.
both sides refused at check 0 (deployed: not_in_set, portal log 21:48:07Z; in-process: absent, no HTTP request)

reading: Primary: 7f3b2f82, above. Refused at check 0: 28 ms. Passed check 0: 421 ms. Same run, same probe, same source.

Support: every pre-fix run, on either side, takes 306-505 ms; the probe reaches the not-found check, which is a warehouse round trip. Every check-0 refusal takes 3 ms in-process and 28-42 ms deployed, an order of magnitude less. The deployed figure is the Apps HTTP round trip with no data access behind it.

For reference, other probes in 47501246 that are refused by input validation, with no data access, take 16-42 ms remote and 2-4 ms in-process (find_cohort limit 51/201 and FY2022: 16-17 ms; classifier_explain bogus task: 24 ms; list_pending_reviews 'nobody': 29 ms; submit_review_request invalid: 39-40 ms). Probes that read the warehouse before failing take 505-1083 ms remote (get_project_detail, classify_parent, get_reviewer_assignment with appl_id 1). The check-0 refusal sits in the first band.
The byte change 163 -> 126 is the not-found message being replaced by the uniform refusal text.
does_not_establish: Not a latency or performance claim: one probe per run, wall-clock, single runs.

Timing cannot exclude a fast, cached or in-memory read. It is consistent with no warehouse access, and the absence of a read rests on the code and the structural test; timing is a second, independent line of evidence for the same ordering.
It covers the tool path (/mcp). For the /operator/decide and agent-approve paths, the order is shown by code and CI only.
